person_note: House Rules uses chapter-length narration by multiple participating characters—Emma, Theo, Jacob, Rich, and Oliver—but the narrators consistently speak as I, so multiple voices do not make the book ALTERNATING under the methodology. The Goodreads evidence independently contains sustained first-person narration attributable to several of those characters, while dialogue, aphorisms, universal you statements, and embedded case material were excluded from the person decision. Authorized excerpts and whole-book structural sources agree that the controlling narration is first person. The context-stripped fragments remain locally unresolved but create no credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person sections.
